newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks due to open flat to higher.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks due to open flat to higher.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were due to open flat to slightly firmer on Tuesday but trading was expected to be defensive ahead of this afternoon's outcome of the Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
U.S. housing starts in July, forecast at 1.46 million annually, a touch higher than in June, were due at 0830 EDT.

"The markets are going to be somewhat on the defensive usually until we hear from the FOMC, though nobody expects them to raise rates," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.
The FOMC's outcome is due around 1815 GMT.

The market will also be scrutinizing the tentative agreement between United Parcel Service and the Teamsters union to end their bitter 15-day strike for its effect on future inflation and corporate earnings.

Union President Ron Carey declared victory and said the Teamsters won sweeping concessions for additional full-time jobs, better union pensions and improved pay that "sends a signal that American workers are on the move again."
Analysts took heart from Monday's late afternoon rebound in the Dow which ended up 108.7 points at 7,803.36.
